Precipue tamen ioram qui dum diceret ut illi molestus non esset sed potius ad prophetas patris sui matrisque properaret quasi illi ueri essent rogabat et supplicabat ut prophetaret et eos qui a periculo liberaret.
Latin.35: Illo uero iurante per deum quia non responderet nisi propter iosaphat sanctum et iustum deducto ad medium quodam homine scientes pallere diuinitus inspiratus, precepit regibus ut in torrente multos lacus effoderent
Latin.36: dicens, neque nube neque spspiritus aliquo flante, imbre diffuso uidebitis fluuium aqua plenum ita ut homines et iumenta uere asitis periculo satientur, et id que uobis non solum deus donabit, sed etiam hostes superabitis, et urbes moabitarum munitissimas capietis, et arbores quidem incidetis pomiferas, et uastabitis prouinciam. Fontes autem fluuiosque damnabitis,
Latin.37: hec dicente propheta, altera die prius quam sol oriretur torrens uehementer influxit. Contigerat enim ut tribus diebus idumea uehemens imbres funderetur, ita ut exercitus iumenta habun dantiaabundantia nimia rigarentur.
Latin.38: Cumque audissent tres reges per desertum contra se uenientes collecto exercitu rex eorum iussit, ut montana exercitus eius adgredere, ne latenter hostes prouinciam inuaderent.
Latin.39: Et cum non esset hebreorum a moabitidis procul exercitus respicientes moabitide ortu solis aquam in torrente sanguine similem suspicati sunt, ut se tres reges inuicem perimissent, et fluuius eorum sanguine redundaret.
Latin.40: Quodcum arbitrati fuissent, petierunt a rege suo ut eos ad spolia hostium destinaret, et impetu facto quasi ad diuinitas preparatas ad inimicorum castra uenerunt et spe sua decepti sunt. Nam circumdantes israhelites alii quidem eorum perempti alii per uniersam prouinciam sunt dispersi.
Latin.41: Tres ergo reges ingredientes moabitarum ciuitates et eas subuerterunt et agros eorum populati sunt et uehementer examinauerunt replentes eos ex lapidibus torrentum et arborum optimas absciderunt, et fontes aquarum pariter obstruxerunt, ac muros usque ad fundamenta deposuerunt.
Latin.42: Rex autem moabitarum dum persecutionem et obsessionem nimiam pateretur, et uideret ciuitatem capi posset in perpetuum, fecit cum septingentis uiris ut inter hostium castra quo possit effugeret quod tamen imperare non potuit. Nam ad quendam locum ueniens ualde munitum dum fugere non ualuisset
Latin.43: reuersus in ciuitatem opus disperationis et crudelis necessitatis impleuit. Filius namque seniorem qui erat ei successurus in regnum eleuans super murum ut a cunctis hostibus uideretur deo immolabit holocaustum. Reges autem uidentes hoc factum eius necessitatis ab urbe misericormisericordia et humana compassione detentionem presumptionis est soluerunt et ad propria remearunt.
Latin.44: Iosaphat autem reuersus in hierosolima in pace degebat, et cum paucum temporis post illud prelium uixisset defunctus est. Qui uixit quidem annis numero sexaginta, imperauit quinque et uiginti, magnificamque meruit in hierosoli mus habere sepulturam similisque fuit magnorum operum dauid.
Latin.45: Reliquid autem filios multos, successorem uero habuit is seniorem filium ioram. Is enim nomen habebat fratris matris suae regis israhelitarum achab,
Latin.46: ueniens autem de regione moabitide rex israhelitarum in samariam habebat heliseum sicut prophetam cuius actos uolo narrare. Sunt enim ualde precipui et historia digni sicut ex libris sacris datur ignosci.
Latin.47: Ad hunc enim cum accessisset uxor obeth dispensatoris achab eique dixisset quia non ignoraret quando uir eius liberasset a morte prophetas dum requisiuit achab uxor iezabel eos occidere et contracto debitoex eis occulte pauisset, et post eius mortem creditoribus urgueretur, atque eius filii ad seruitium deducerentur. Ob quam rem rogabat ut eius meriti miseretur operibus et aliquid solacium ad necessitatem preberet.
Latin.48: Qui dum requisisset siquid haberet in domo aliud nihil esse sibi respondit nisi paruum uas olei. Tunc propheta precepit ut multa uasa uacua sibimet a uicinis acommodaret, et clausis ianuis domus suae ex illo oleo in omnia uasa defunderet,
Latin.49: que cum completa fuissent omnia et nullum uacuum remansisset, ueniens ad prophetam nuntiauit hoc ei.
Latin.50: Ille uero consilium dedit ut oleum uendiderit et pretium creditoribus daret, et ex ipso olei pretio recti in quo aut recti iudicabitis.
Latin.111: quibus festinantibus ut audirent atque rogantibus ait ad eum dixisse quia ipse fuerit electus a deo rex, hec itaque dum dixisset unus quisque exuens se quod habuerat uestes ei propria substernebant. Et mittentes tubas ieuhieu regem esse clamabant.
Latin.112: Ille uero exercitu congregato pergebat ad ioram in ciuitatem iezrahel in qua sicut prediximus pro uulnere curandus abierat quam coeperat cum obsederat aramach. Contigit autem ut eo tempore hierosolimitarum rex ochodias uenisset ad ioram. Erat enim filius sororis eius sicut dudum diximus ut uisitaret eum propter uulnus quod in obsessione conceperat,
Latin.113: hieu autem subito uolens super ioram inruere  rogauit ut nullus militum descendens regi ioram quae gesta fuerant nuntiaret dicens, hanc esse maximam eorum circa se deuotionem si eum regem hoc ordine demonstrarent.
Latin.114: Illi uero in his quae fuerant dicta gratanter itinera conseruabant, nequis latenter pergens quod gestum fuerat indicaret. Et hieu quidem sumptis equitibus electis sedens in curru ibat in iezrahel. Cumque proximus fuerit ciuitati explorator quem rex constituerat ioram ut ad ciuitatem uenientes inspexerit. Uidens cum multitudine ueniente hieu nuntiauit ioram regi uidere se equites uenientes.
Latin.115: Ille uero repente aliquem mitti iussit equestrium qui ei occurreret, et quis esset agnosceret. Qui dum uenisset ad hieu de exercitu requisiuit dicens a rege semissum. At ille nihil de his respondens requirenti sequi iussit.
Latin.116: Quod dum explorator uidisset indicauit ioram, quod qui fuerat missus equestris mixtus multitudini ueniret una cum eis. Iterum rege mittente etiam alium hoc cum facere hieu imperauit.
Latin.117: Quod dum explorator ioram indicasset nouissime in curru ipse conscendens cum ochodia hierosolimorum rege in eius occursum egressus est,
Latin.118: hieu autem cum multa moderatione et disciplina agebat iter. Cumque ioram uenisset in agrum nabuthei requirebat si in exercitu recte omnia gererentur, et cum ei hieu amarissime malediceret matrem eius ueneficam meretricemque clamaret, metuens rex, et nihil eum cogitaret quod esset salubre credens, conuerso curru suo ut poterat fugiebat dicens ad ochoziam eo quod insidiis et dolo fuisset captus, hieu autem sagittam post eum mittens eius cor suo laculo penetrabit.
Latin.119: Et ioram quidem repente cadens flexu poplite animam de reliquid, heu autem continuo iussit uadacro principi tertie partis ut corpus ioram in agro proleceret nabuthei, recordans prophetiam heliae quam patri eius qui fuit interfector nabuthei praedixerat quam et ipse et eius genus in illius agro periret.
Latin.120: Hec enim eum sederet, tunc postergum currus achab audisse se propheta narrante dicebat. Quod etiam secundum illius prouenit eloquium, igitur eaden te ioram metuens ochonias de sua salute curruum in alia itineris parte conuertit, credens qualiter effugeret hieu.
Latin.121: Ille uero perfectus est cum ad quodam ascensu conprehendens sagittam eodem emissa eum percussit, qui derelicto curru ascendens in equo fugit, hieu in macedon ibique curatus post paucum uulneris illius tempus et ipse defunctus est, portans in hierosolimorum illic sepultus est, cum regnasset anno uno. Fuit enim malignus et plus ualde quam pater eius.
Latin.122: Cum autem hieu intrasset in iezrahelem urbem, zezabel ornata stans supra turrem. Bonus in quid seruus qui occidit dominum suum, ille ue re respiciens ad eam quę est interrogauit, et descendentem ad se uenire precepit. Nouissime uero eunuchis imperauit ut eam de terraeterra deicerent.
Latin.123: Quę dum precepitata fuisset murum sanguine suo aspersit et concultata equorum pedibus expirauit, his ita gestis hieu ingressus palatium cum suis amicis et semet ipsum reficiebat et illos conuiuiis aliis rebus precepit que famulis quia zezabel per imerent, et eam propter decus generis sepelirent. Erat enim ex regibus
Latin.124: sed nihil de eius corpore quibus hoc imperatum fuerat in uenerunt nisi tantumodo summitates. Aliud uero tantum corpus a canibus est adsumptum. Haec audiens hieu heliae prophetiam nimis obstipuit. Is enim in iezrahela praedixerat hac eum in teritu fore perituram.
Latin.125: Inter ea dum achab filii septuaginta in samaria nutrirentur, misit hieu duas epistolas aliam principibus samaritanorum dicens, ut fortissimum filium achab constituerent regem eum et curros haberent multos et equos et arma ad militia et ciuitates munitas, quod dum facerent domino suo repensarent,
Latin.126: haec autem scripsit uolens samaritanorum mentes agnoscere. Relegentes uero litteras hae petagogiapaedagogia timuerunt exagitantes quod nihil possent contra eum facere, qui magis duobus praeualisset imperiis scripserunt profitentes se eum habere dominum et facere quecumque preciperet.
Latin.127: Ille uero ad haec rescripsit praecipiens ut si oboedirent et filiorum achab abscidentes capita destinarent. Tunc principes euocantes nutritores infantum iusserunt ut occidentes eos capita eorum absciderent et mitterent ad hieu, haec illi nihil resistentes egerunt et conponentes in quibusdam uasculis de uimine factis eorum capita destinarent,
Latin.128: his autem allatis ad hieu cum amicis cenanti nuntiatum est, quod capita filiorum achab uiderentur esse delata, qui iussit ante portam ex utraque parte ex eis capitibus aggeres fieri,
Latin.129: factoque die ad ea uidenda processit, et inspiciens dicere coepit ad populum, quia ipse quidem contra suum dominum militasset, et illum per imisset, hos autem omnis non ipse permiserit eosque cognoscere deposcebat de generatione achab, quia omnia secumdum dei prophetam fuerant gesta, et domus eius sicut helias praedixerat deperisset.
Latin.130: Cumque necasset eos qui apud iezrahelitas ex achab genere sunt inuenti, cum equis ad samariam properabat. Per iter autem inueniens aliquos ochodiae hierosolimitarum regis interrogauit eos quo properarent.
Latin.131: Illi uero dicentes quia uenerint ut ioram salutarent, et regem suum ochodiam nescientes quod ambo ab eo occisi fuissent, hieus autem eos conprehensos praecepit occidi, erant etiam numero quadraginta et duo.
Latin.132: Post haec autem occurrit ei uir quidam bonus et iustus ionadab olim amicus eius, quicum salutasset eum coepit laudare eo quod omnia cum dei uoluntate fecisset et achab genus exterminasset,
Latin.133: hieu autem rogabit ut ascendens in currum ad samariam cum eo ueniret ei se demonstraturum dicens, quod nulli parceret malignantium, sed et falsos prophetas et falsos sacerdotes, et suadentes plebi ut magni quidem dei religionem desererent et extraneos adorarent in se puniret. Cum esset utique optima nimis haec inspectio atque gratissima et bonus et iustus uir uiderit malos tormentis affligi,
Latin.134: his consenti eris ionadab ascendens in currum uenit pariter in samariam. Hieu autem requirens omnes cognatos achab interfecit. Uolens autem nullum de falsis prophetis neque de sacerdotibus idolorum achab supplicum declinaret, deceptionem quadam et dolo conprehendit uniuersos
Latin.135: congregato siquidem populo dixit, uelle se duplices deos introductos quam achab colebat adoraret ro grans ut eos sacerdotes et prophetae et serui pariter aduenirent, quatenus copiosa sacrificia et precipuas diis achab hostias immolaret et esset morte multandus, sacerdos qui tunc non fuerit inuentus deus achab baal appellabatur.
Latin.136: Constituens itaque diem quo uelit sacrificia celebrare missis in omnem israhelitarum regione nuntiis, qui ad illum baal sacerdotes adducerent, quibus pariter congregatis iussit hieu pontifici ut daret omnibus uestes eisque sumentibus ingressus in domum cum amico suo ionadab, praecepit ut cum diligentia quaererentur ne quis, inter eos alienigena aut peregrinus inueniretur, cum nollet sacerdotibus idolorum alius inter esse fidelium.
Latin.137: Illis uero dicentibus nullum inter esse peregrinum et inchoantibus sacrificia celebrare constituit a foris octuaginta milia numero uiros armatos quos nouerat fidelissimos, iussitque eis ut falsos prophetas occiderent, et ipsi in paterna sollempnitate permanerent, quam multo iam tempore distitissent, et simul interminatus est ut siqui effugerint pro illis animas eorum auferret.
Latin.138: Illi uero et omnes uiros interimerunt et domum baal igne concremauerunt, et hoc modo a peregrinis sollempnitatibus samaria liberarunt, hic itaque baal tyriorum fuerat deus. Achab autem uolens parere socero iobal, qui rex tyriorum tunc erat et sidonis templum ei fecit in samaria sacerdotesque instituit et omni eos cultura religionis honorauit.
Latin.139: Cum igitur hic deos fuisset exterminans, aureos tamen uitulos hieu israhelitas adorare permisit, haec autem dum fecisset pro imperii castigationibus castigasset, deus ei per prophetam predixit eo quod in quattuor generationibus super israhel essent eius filii regnaturi. Igitur circa hieu talia gerebantur.
Latin.140: Gotholia uero achab filia audiens ioram fratris sui mortem et ochozie filii et totius generis regum unam perditionem studiuit, ut nullum de dauid domo relinquerent, sed omne genus exterminaret, ut nullus ex eis ad regnum ulterius perueniret,
Latin.141: et hoc quidem sicut potuit fecit. Euasit autem unus filius ochodiae mortem hoc modo diffugiens. Ochodias ex uno patre habuit sororem nomine iosabere, cui copulatus erat pontifex ioda,
Latin.142: haec ingressa regiam domum ubi erant interfecti filii regum, ioas nomine infantulum anniculum celatum inueniens cum nutrice et portans incubiculum clausit, et latenter aluit ipsa et uir eius ioda in templo sex annis quibus in hierosolimis super duos tribus gotholia regnauit.
Latin.143: Septimo uero anno ioda hunc sermone pandidit quinque uiris centurionibus eisque suasit ut consisterent contra ea quae ago dolia fuerant perpetrata, et regnum infanti traderent, percepturus ab eis iure iurandum quod securitas talia gerentibus praepararetur prodidit eis quae gerenda forent atque complenda.
Latin.144: Tunc uiri quibus sacerdos iodam suum consilium comiserat circum euntes omnem prouinciam sacerdotes et leuitas congregantes ex ea simul et principes tribum omnes hierosolimis ad pontificem deduxerunt.
Latin.145: Qui mox fidem ab eis cum iure iurando petit, ut quod ab eo cognoscerent cum taciturnitate seruarent. Donec nisus eius intentionis potuisset impleri. Quibus iurantibus securum effectum deducens eum, quem degenere dauid de nutrierat. Iste in quid uobis rex ex illa domo erit quam nostis deum prophetasse super nos omni tempore regnaturam,
Latin.146: moneo siquidem ut tertiam partem uestram eum custodire faciatis in templo. Quartam uero in omnibus templi ianuis statuatis. Reliqua uero pars teneat portam quae ducit ad tecta regalia. Alia in armis multitudo consistat in templo nullumque armatum permittatis intrare, nisi tantu modo sarcerdotes,
Latin.147: eis quoque praecepit ut pars aliqua sacerdotum et leuitarum circa ipsum regem adsisteret eum euaginatis gladiis circumdantes, ut siquis armatus in templum intrare presumeret repente perimeretur,
Latin.148: et nihil metuentes regem tamen fortiter obseruarent. Illi uero consilio pontificis oboedientes suam uoluntatem opera declararunt inter iodas aperientes armamentum quod erat in templo a dauid constitutum diuisit centurionibus et sacerdotibus pariter et leuitis arma quaecumque illic inuenit lanceas et faretra, et quod cumque aliud adprehendit genus armatorum et armatos circa templum statuit, ut manu sua totum constipare uiderentur ingressum, et quasi murum habitate studi nemolentur
Latin.149: percipientes que in medio puerum ei regnum diadema posuerunt et unguens eum iodam regem sollempniter ordinauit. Populus itaque gaudens clamauit uiuat rex.
Latin.150: Porro godolia tumultum et laudes inopinabiles repente cognoscens uehementer perturbata cum suo exercitu de regalibus exiliuit. Et cum uenisset ad templum sacerdotes quidem eam protinus exceperunt armatos uero qui sequebantur introire prohiberunt. Erant enim a pontifice proposita sicut dictum est, ut templi aditus obseruarent.
Latin.151: Tunc itaque godolia uidens puerum stantem super tribunal regum eique diadema regale super inpositum, scissa ueste sua uehemens exclamans iussit occidi qui ei fecerat insidias et principatum auferre temptabat. Iodam uero euocans centuriones iussit ut educentes godoliam in conualle cedron eam ibi perimerent, ne templum occidentes illic ueneficam uiolarent
Latin.152: unum praecipiens ut siquis ei ferre uelit auxilium pari sorte perimeretur. Tunc quidem cui fuerat eius in iuncta peremptio sumens godoliam deduxit eam ad portam mularum regis et illicinterfecit.
Latin.153: Cum ergo godolia fuissent gesta conuocans populum et armatos ioadas in templum coniurauit omnes ut rega fauerent et eius saluti prospexerint, quando in deuotione regia deum potius honorarent, et ne transcenderent mos eos leges. Ius iurandum quoque conpulit exhibere,
Latin.154: post hoc concurrentes ad domum baal quam godolia et ioram uir eius instruxerat ad iniuriam paterni dei et honorem achab eam funditus euerterunt, et sacerdotem eius mathan nomine perimerunt.
Latin.155: Diligenta uero atque templi custodiam sacerdotes et leuitas ioada habere permittit, et secundum regis dauid praeceptum iussit eos secundo in die holocausta et sacrificia sollempniter immolare ut secundum legem incensum ferent. Fecit autem et quosdam leuitarum portarios ad templi munimen, ne illic fordidum aliquid latenter intraret.
Latin.156: Haec itaque uniuersa disponens cum centurionibus et omni populo sumens puerum de templo, ioadas eum cum uniuersis ad regalia usque perduxit, quo in regio solio residente cunctus populus cum fauore sollempniter ad clamauit, et ad epulas conuersi simul festiuitatem multis diebus egerunt. Ciuitas ergo quedam habebat godoliam de rebus humanis ablatam.
Latin.157: Ioas itaque adeptus regnum erat annorum septem cuius mater fuit nomine sabia ex regione bersabe multamque habuit custodiam legum et culturam diuine religionis exhibuit omni temporem quo uixit ioada
Latin.158: aetate uero congrua duxit uxores duas dante sibi pontifice ex quibus et masculi ei et femine nate sunt. Igitur de rege ioas et quem ad modum insidias godoliae defugerit regnum que percoeperit his indicasse sufficiat.
Latin.159: Azrahel autem syrorum rex dum pugaret contra israhelitas et contra regem eorum hieu uastauit prouinciam trans iordanen quae erat ad orientem tribus ruben et gaad et mannasse et galaad et bathan eam percurrens ubique et cuncta diripiens eum resistentibus inferens uniuersis
Latin.160: in quo potuit quidem ulcisci hieudum cunctam prouinciam deuastaret, sed circa diuinitatem superbus et contempto resistens et legitima sancta despiciens mortuus est, cum regnasset super israhelitas annis septem et uiginti. Sepultus est autem in samaria successorum principatum ioathan filium derelinquens.
Latin.161: Regem uero hierosolimorum ioas quodam desiderium adpraehenderat ut templum innouaret. Quodam die euocans pontificem ioadam, iussit ut in omnem mitteret regionem et leuitaset sacerdotes exigeret pro unius cuiusque capite dimidium sidi argenti ad fabricam et renouationem templi quod a ioram et godoliam et eorum filiis uidebatur esse destructum.
Latin.162: Pontifex autem hoc equidem non fecit sciens quod nullus conferret argentum. Tertio uero et uigesimo anno regni sui ioas euocans ad ipsum et leuitas et quasi in oboedientes sui praecepti culpans iussit ut pro hac re in futuro anno pro renouatione templi prospicerent. Quo facto consilio pontifex usus est pro congregatione pecuniarum quod populus libenter habuit et gratanter impleuit.
Latin.163: Fecit namque ligeam arcam et undique muniens eam unum ei foramen aperiens quam ponens in templo iuxta sacrarium iussit singulos quantum uellent in eam mittere perforamen pro templi reparatione. Ad hoc igitur opus omnis populus libenter accessit, et multum argenti multum auri largitus est.
Latin.164: Quo facto euacuantes arcam rege praesente scriba simul et sacerdos gazo fila ciorum dinumerantes quod fuerat congregatum. Deinde eandem arcam in ipso loco reposuerunt, et hoc diebus singulis faciebant. Cumque populus quod ei fuerat uisum obtulisset, miserunt pontifices ioades et rex ioas ut cesores lapidum instructores que conducerent et ligna maxima de optima silua deponerent.
Latin.165: Templo siquidem reparato aurum quod remanserat et argentum non paruum ad pateras et uini fusoria, et coopercula et uasa religua deportarunt sacrificiis quae cottidie adolentes alta redigebant.Et haec quidem tempore quo aduixit ioadas conpetenti studio gerebantur.
Latin.166: Cum uero mortuus fuisset qui uixerat annis centum et triginta, iustus et per omnia uenerandus et sepultus fuisset in hierosolimis in regiis monumentis, quem generis dauid repararat imperium. Rex ioas curam perdidit diuinae religionis,
Latin.167: cumquo etiam primatus plebis pariter uitiati sunt, ut circa sollemnitates et legitima iura delinquerent. Deus autem dure ferens transgressionem regis et aliorum misit prophetas qui contestarentur eos ut ab huius modi gestorum malignitate retederent.
Latin.168: Illi uero in tali malorum more et desiderio permanserunt, ut nec alios qui ante se propter legitimorum iniurias fuerant castigati, neque prophetas qui praedicebant ut penitentiam agerent, et conuerterentur ab iniquitate respicerent. Nam et zachariam filium pontificis ioade lapidibus in templo rex iussit occidi beneficiorum patris eius oblitus.
Latin.169: Quem cum deus prophetam constituisset stans in media multitudine suadebat eis simul et regi ut iustitiam facerent. Et quod magna supplicia susciperent si nollent dei praeceptionibus oboedire. Qui tamen cum moreretur suarum passionum testem deum et iudicem proclamauit, quia pro bono consilio et pro his quae pater eius praestiterat regi ioas ille amare et uiolenter occumberet.
Latin.170: Rex autem non post multum temporis spatium iustissimas poenas horum in quibus preuaricatus est exsoluit. Ueniente namque azahel syrorum rege in eius prouinciam et geth deuastante atque depopulante. Cum esset iam ad hierosolima deducturus exercitus. Metuens ioas obsessionem euacuatis omnibus dei thesauris atque regalibus et ministerium templi misit syrorum regi his eum redimens ne ciuitas pateretur pressionem aut periculum rerum omnium sustinuerit.
Latin.171: Cui dum satisfactum fuisset ingenti multitudine pecuniarum nequaquam ad hierosolima castra metatus est. Ioas tamen cum pessimum languorem incurrisset et instantes amici qui mortem zachariae ioadas filii defendebant eique insidias facientes interimerunt eum,
Latin.172: et sepultus est quidem in hierosolimis. Non autem in monumentis patrum quod fuerat inimicus et diuine religionis inimicus. Uixit autem annos quidem septem et quadraginta, in eius autem imperio successit eius filius amasias.
Latin.173: Uigesimo et primo anno regni ioas israhelitarum principatum potitus est, ioachaz filius hieu in samaria quem et habuit annis septem et decem. Patris quidem sui nec ipse imitatur existens, impie uero gerens sicut et primi reges qui deum spreuisse uidebantur.
Latin.174: Hunc autem humiliauit asel et extanta equitibus castra mouisset. Nam et ciuitates ei plurimas et maximas abstulit et eius milites trucidauit.
Latin.175: Haec itaque passus est israhelitarum populus secundum helisei prophetiam quando azahel qui occidit dominum suum regnaturum esse praedixerat super syros et damascenos. Cumque ioachaz in his anxietatibus tenetur a preces dei supplicationes que confugit, rogans ut eum de azahel manibus liberaret nec pateretur ut sub illius eum ditione uideretur.
Latin.176: Deus autem poenitentiam pro uirtute suscipiens et corripere magis quam perdere hominem huius modi uolens concessit ei quatenus belli pericula declinaret. Pace itaque potita prouincia rursum ad statum pristinum copiamque regressa est.
Latin.177: Post mortem uero achaz filius eius ioas suscepit regnum cum septem iam et triginta annos haberet in regno, iosias super tribum iuda tenuit principatum, iste ioas in samaria super populum israhelis. Nam et ipse idem habebat nomen quod hierosolimorum rex. Tenuitque regnum annis sedecim,
Latin.178: fuit que bonus et in nullo paternae naturae consimilis. Illo quidem tempore dum helisei prophetia in senectute consisteret ut egritudinem incurrisset. Uenit israhelitarum rex uisitaturus eum
Latin.179: et dum eum innouissimis inuenisset flere coepit eo uidente et ingemescere patrem eum uocare et secutum se regnum propter eum dicens. Numquamcontra hostes armis egisse sed illos prospere sine dimicatione uicisse, qui tum auita disceret haec hebraei syris relinquerint, et aliis inimicis captiuandos
Latin.180: qua propter nec ipsam uitam securam ulterius fore dicebat sed gratum sibi esse ut cum eo a presente luce redeceret, haec dicente atque gemente rege, heliseus consolabatur eum iussitque ut ad latum sibimet arcum extenderet. Qui cum praeparasset arcum contingens manus eius propheta iussit ut sagittaret.
Latin.181: Cumque tres sagittas dimisisset aque cessasset ait. Si plures dimisisset eradicasses syrorum regnum. Quod uero in tribus solum modo quieuistis, totiens congressus syris pugnando praeualebis, ut regionem quam abstulerunt atuo patre rursus obtineas. Et rex quidem dum haec audisset abscessit.
Latin.182: Post non multum uero tempus et propheta defunctus est, uir iustitia famosissimus et in dei studiis ualde predarus, miraculum namque et inopinabilia opera per suas prophetas ostendit, et apud hebraeos memoriam claram et magnificam sepulturam habere promeruit, et qualem uiro ita religioso decebat inpendi,
Latin.183: illo siquidem tempore contigit ut quidam latrones in helisei sepulchrum mortuum quem ipsi uidebantur inter fecisse proiecerint. Cum cadauer dum eius fuisset corpori sociatum continuo suscitatum est, et de heliseo quod est propheta et quecumque predixit, et quomodo post mortem uirtutem diuinam habuit, haec declarata sufficiant.
Latin.184: Defuncto itaque rege syrorum azahel ad filium eius addan peruenit imperium, contra quem ioas israhelitarum rex dimicaret et cum tribus congressionibus eum uincens omnem prouinciam ab eo retraxit, et quascumque ciuitates et uicos eius, pater azahel de israhelitarum regno subtraxerat liberauit.
Latin.185: Hoc itaque secundum prophetiam helisei prouenit. Cumque contigisset ut etiam ioas moreretur, ille quidem sepultus est in samaria, regnum uero suo filio gessoban nomine dereliquid.
Latin.186: Anno secundo ioas regis israhelitarum regnauit super tribum iuda in hierosolimis. Amasias cuius mater erat nomine ioad, in genere uero ciuis et iustitiae prouisione mirabilis, qui cum iuuenis esset et ueniens ad regnum cogitauit ut inimicos qui patrem eius occiderant puniret
Latin.187: et conprehensos omnes occidit, filiis autem, eorum pepercit sequens mos eos leges qui non sanciuit propter peccata parentum filios occidendos.
Latin.188: Deinde eligens exercitum de tribu iuda et beniamin qui flore iuuentutis et circa uiginti annos ex his congregans quasi triginta milia constituit super eos centuriones, mittens que ad regem israhelitarum conduxit argentum talentis centum milia armatorum. Deliberauerat enim ut amalechitarum gentibus et idumeis et gabanitis inferret bellum.
Latin.189: Cumque praepararetur ad bellum etiam uideretur positus in procinctu, suasit ei propheta ut dimitteret israhelitarum exercitum quod esset impius et deus cum uinci praedicaret utique suorum solum modo solacio uteretur et hostibus praeualeret, cum paucis contra eos uolente deo pugnando.
Latin.190: Cumque grauiter hoc ferret rex eo quod mercedes israhelitis iam praebuisset in gentes, monebat propheta ut ageret quod deo placeret, cum possent pecunia ex ipsius muneribus abundare, et illos quidem dimisit cedens quas dederat rex mercedes. Ipse uero cum suo exercitu ad praedictas gentes accessit
Latin.191: et proelio gesto uincens decem milia quidem occidit et totidem uiuos coepit eosque ducens ad magnam petram quę est in arabia constituta ex ea praecipitauit. Praedam uero et diuitias ex his gentibus abstulit infinitas.
Latin.192: Dum itaque in his amasias consisteret israhelitę quos cum mercede data admiserat indignati et credentes iniuriam quod quos uituperatione fuissent ab eo remissi eius regni terras adgressi sunt, et usque betheron procedentes deripuere prouinciam et multa quidem abstulere iumenta et triamilia hominum occiderunt.
Latin.193: Amasias autem uictoria ex his quae gesta fuerant eleuatus, quidem qui ei horum omnium auctor extiterit, coepit peruenire ad deos illos quos de amalechitarum prouincia uexerat adorare.
Latin.194: Tunc accedens propheta mirari se dixit cum eos rex deos arbitraretur adorandos, qui suos et a quibus honorabantur iuuare non potuissent, nec ab huius manibus liberassent. Sed pereuntes defendere contempsissent, et ipsi quoque in hierosolima ad instar hostium captiuorum uincti deducti fuissent.
Latin.195: Haec itaque regi mouerunt iram et praecepit ut deberent dicere ad prophetam in terminatus eum se puniturum si amplius loqueretur et propheta quidem tacere se dixit, praedicens non esse praebiturum deum ea quae rex facere moliretur.
Latin.196: Amasias uero dum abstinere se non possit in rebus felicibus constitutus quas a deo perciperat eique faciebat iniurias scripsit ad regem israhelitarum ioas ut obaudiret ei et ipse et populus uniuersus sicut prius obaudiebant parentibus eius dauid et salomoni, quis ipa rere nollent scirent quod bellum terminum causa perciperet.
Latin.197: Cui iosias rex ita rescripsit. Rex ioas regi amasiae erat in libano monte cypressus omnino poterat et puluis exinde misit ad cypressum petens filiam eius filio suo daret uxorem, et dum haec ageret bestia quaedam transiens puluerem conculcauit,
Latin.198: hoc ergo tibi erit exemplum ut maiora non appetas ne quem amalechitas uicisti in hoc exultans tibi tuo regno uidearis in ferri pericula,
Latin.199: haec autem relegens amasias ad bellum potius incitatus est deo arbitror ad hoc in pellente ut prohis quae fuerant ab eo commissa poenas ex solueret. Cumque produxisset exercitum contra ioas et esset iam proelium commissurus milites amasię repentinus terror et stupor inuasit, qualem non propitius deus inmittet,
Latin.200: et ante quam uenirent ad manus in fugam animi pauore conuersi sunt. Illis igitur terroribus dispersis contigit ut amasias desolatus ab hostibus caperetur, eique ioas mortem interminatus est ne hierosolimitis suaderet ut aperientes portas eum cum exercitu in ciuitate susciperent.
Latin.201: Et amasias quidem mortis terrore conpulsus suscipere fecit. Hostem qui destruens partem muri, quasi quadringentorum cubitorum, cum curru ingressus est hierosolima, amasiam captiuum ducens
Latin.202: et dominus hoc modo hierosolimitane ciuitati effectus, et dei thesaurum abstulit et aurum argentumque quod in amasię regalibus erat exhausit, et ita eum a captiuitate resoluens regressus est ad samariam.
Latin.203: Haec itaque gesta sunt circa hierosolimitas anno quarto et decimo regis amasię, qui post haec passus insidias amicorum, fugit quidem in ciuitate lachis. Interfectus est autem ab eis mittentibus qui eum illic interimerunt, cuius corpus referentes in hierosolima regaliter tutauerunt.
Latin.204: Igitur amasias hoc modo si niuit uitam propter superbiam et contemptam quem habuit circa deum qui uixit quidem annis quattuor et quinquaginta, regnauit autem uiginti nouem huic successit filius suus nomine ozias.
Latin.205: Anno autem quinto decimo regni amasię regnauit in israhel filius ioas hieroboam in samaria annis quadraginta, hic autem rex circa deum quidem iniuriosus et iniquus extitit uehementer idola colenda in multa incongrua et opera extranea faciendo, populo autem israhelitarum multorum fuit occasio,
Latin.206: huic quidem ionas prophetauit quod oporteret eum syros uincere dimicantem et regnum proprium dilatare, in partibus quidem aquilonis usque ad emachi ciuitatem a meridie uero usque ad aspaltiden.
Latin.207: Antiquitus enim termini cananei isti fuerunt sicut principes hiesus ea loca determinauit, igitur hieroboam castra metatus contra syros omnem eorum prouinciam sicut ionas prophetauerat deuastauit.
Latin.208: Necessarium uero iudicaui integritatem rerum contradere studens quaecumque et de isto propheta in sacris libris inueni conscripta omnia declarare, hic enim iussus a deo ut iret ad nineue regnum et ibidem predicaret quod esset amissuraciuitas principatum metuens non perrexit sed fugit deum in ioppe, et inuenta naue ingressus in tarsum ciuitate ciliciae nauigabat.
Latin.209: Cumque tempestas inmineret asperrime nauis submersionis pericula sustineret. Naute quidem et gubernator et ipse nauclerius fundebant orationes quatenus periculum maris euaderent, ionas autem operiens semetipsum iacebat et nihil emitabatur horum quae uidebat efficere.
Latin.210: Cumque tempestas potius augeretur et uiolentius uentorum nimietate mare at tolleretur in cumulum. Cogitantes simul quia aliquis nauigantium huius tempestatis auctor existeret, constituerunt ut quicumque his esset sorte proiceretur.
Latin.211: Quibus hoc facientibus sors cecidit in prophetam. Interrogantibus autem illis unde esset et quod ageret genere se quidem dixit hebraeum, prophetam uero summi dei eisque suasit, ut si uellent praesens periculum declinare eum in pelagum proicerent, quod tempestatis eorum auctor existeret.
Latin.212: Et illi quidem prius non hoc facere presumpserunt, impium iudicantes sipere grinum hominem et qui eis suam commiserat salutem ad haec mala complerent, cum utique non dum nauis submersio prouenisset. Prophetam uero post haec conpulsi et timore suae salutis astricti eum in pelagus proiecerunt,
Latin.213: et tempestas quidem remota est. Illi uero sermo est quod a coeto deuoratus post tres dies totidemque noctes in euxino portu uiuus euomitus est. In nulla parte corporis maculatus,
Latin.214: qui supplicans deo ut ei ueniam concederet pro delicto ad niniue profectus et ciuitatem, et instans in medio praedicauit, quod post breuissimum tempus asiae perderent principatum, haec ergo eis indicans est reuersus. Haec itaque nar nationem explicui sicut scriptum inueni.
Latin.215: Igitur hieroboam rex cum omni felicitate uitam degens et regnans annis quadraginta defunctus est et sepultus in samaria cui successit in regnum filius zacharias.
Latin.216: Eodem uero modo et ozias amasiae filius, quarto  Hoc ergo tibiiam et decimo anno regni hieroboam duabus tribus in hierosolimis imperauit, cuius mater fuit athelamas nomine, genere uero ciuis. Erat autem hic bonus et naturaliter iustus atque magnanimus et ad rerum prouidentiam nimis industrius.
Latin.217: Castra uero metatus contra palestinos eos que bello deuincens ciuitates eorum coepit, geth, et iamnias, et muros eorum destruit. Post hanc uero militiam adgressus est arabias uicino aegyptiis, et aedificans ciuitatem circa mare rubrum constituit in ea custodiam.
Latin.218: Deinde ammanitas subdens et tributa eis inponens et omnium quae ad terminos aegyptiorum suę dicione subiciens coepit de cetero hierosolimitarum habere curam. Nam quicumque muri fuerant longo tempore a regum priorum desidia iam destructi eos rursus aedificauit et reparauit, nec non et quoscumque destruxerat israhelitarum rex quando patrem eius amasiam captiuum tenens ingressus fuerat ciuitatem.
Latin.219: Aedificauit autem et turres multas singulis quibusque centum et quinquaginta cubitos habentibus. Fecit que et in desertis magnas ualde munitiones, et multos aquae ductos instuens, habebat autem iumentorum et aliorum animalium in numera multitudinem quando et prouincia fertilis erat ad pascua.
Latin.220: Erat que praecipue terrae cultor et curam habebat circa plantationes et femina fructuum diuersorum. Exercitum uero circa se habuit electorum trecenti septuaginta milia uirorum quorum duces et tribuni et millenarii erant ualde fortissimi, et qui suo robore possent ferri duo milia.
Latin.221: Constituit autem per cohortes totum exercitum et omnes armauit, dans unicuique iaculaturam et scutum et luricasloricas aereas et arcos et splendonas. Super hęc autem et multa machina merita ab ob pressiones instituit quibus petre dimitterentur et iaculata pagones et his similia praeparauit.
Latin.222: Dumque haec ita constituisset mittens elatione corruptus et substancia mortali ditatus contra inmortale omni tempore agere nitebatur. Est autem inmortalis substantia pietas circa deum et custodia mandatorum.
Latin.223: Lapsus est itaque felicitatis euentu, et ad paterna peccata descendit, quae etiam illum post quam claritatem bonorum et rerum magnitudinem de reliquid adprehenderunt. Hic enim in stante insigne die et generali festiuitate, indutus stola sacerdotali intrauit in templum oblaturus incensum in aureo altare deo.
Latin.224: Pontifice uero azaria eum aliis octuaginta sacerdotibus eum prohibentem ne faceret, quoniam haec solummodo his adiacerent qui ex genere aaron erant et clamantibus ei ut exiret et non ageret contra dei leges, iratus interminatus est eis mortem nisi tacerent,
Latin.225: inter haec autem terrae motus factus est magnus et stupes cente populo claritas sols nimis effulsit, et incidit in faciem regis, et illi quidem lepra continuo prouenit. Ante ciuitatem uero in loco quae dicitur eroge scissa est media pars montem ad occidentem et sua uolubilitate per quattuor stadia procedens ad orientalem restitit montem ita ut et uiasuiras clauderet et regios urbes obprimeret.
Latin.226: Cumque sacerdotes regis faciem lepram adprehendisse, conspiciunt, pandebant ei calamitatem suam hortantes ut tamquam pollutus exiret a ciuitate, ille uero confusione huius euentus, et dum illi iam esset nulla fiducia quod iuuebat impleuit, qui licet fuisset ultra humanos mentes de uatus, et propter hoc impie gressisset in deo miserabilem tantum hanc et uilem protulit passionem,
Latin.227: et tempus quidem aliquod extra ciuitatem commoratus in uita priuata de gens filio licet eius suspiciente regnum. Deinde mestitia faciente defunctus est qui uixit quidem annis octo et sexaginta, regnauit quinquaginta et duo, supultus est autem solus in hortis,
Latin.228: zacharias autem filius hieroboam dum mensibus sex regnasset in israhel dolum passus occisus est a quodam amico nomine sellis mo filio iotauis qui post eum regno percepto non amplius quam diebus trigninta tenuit regnum.
Latin.229: Princeps enim militiae manaen illo tempore cum esset in ciuitate tharsi, et audierat quod de zacharia fuerat gestum, surgens inde cum omni militia uenit in samariam, et commisso praelio sellin permitet semetipsum constituens regem
Latin.230: quem suscipere noluerunt. Ille uero ulciscens in eis et quae foris erant depopulatus est, et ciuitatem obsessione fortissima accepit
Latin.231: et grauiter ferens quod fecerunt eius ciues omnes simul occidit, neque paruulis parcens, et quicquid ad culmen pertinebat ferocitatis et seuitia non reliquid. Nam quod alienigene capientes eos facere potuissent. hoc iste de suis contribulibus operatus est.
Latin.232: Itaque manaen hoc more regnauit annis decem, fuit que peruersus et rerum omnium ualde seuissimus. Dum qui aduersus eum castra mouisset phoialus assyriorum rex, ad certamina quidem contra assyrios non accessit, sed mittens eis mille argenti talenta egit ut bello discederet.
Latin.233: Ad hanc itaque causam profuit populus a regi manaen. Nam unusquisque pro capite suo quinquaginta praebuit dragmas. Post haec uero defunctus est et sepultus in Samaria. Phaceam uero suum filium successorem regni proprii dereliquid qui sequens paternam crudelitatem duobus tantummodo regnauit annis.
Latin.234: Deinde in conuiuio dolo cum amicis proprius est peremptus. Phaceas enim millenarius filius romilliae ei fecit insidias quae et ipse phaceas tenuit annis principatum uiginti, fuit autem impius et iniquus.
Latin.235: Rex autem assyriorum theglaphassar nomine castra metatus aduersus israhelitas et cuncta galatidem regionem uastans et transiordanem et quae galiliani cupa tui et trasa et arasan et habitatores una captiuos ducens eos in regno suo migrauit. Igitur ei de assyriorum rege hoc nos declarasse sufficiat.
Latin.236: Ioathan itaque oziae filius regnauit in ierosolimis super tribum iuda cuius mater fuit ciuis quae uocabatur itrasis. Is autem rex nulla uirtute minor fuit sed et rebus quidem diuinis pius. Apud homines autemiustus stabat, habuitque curam rerum ciui uitatis
Latin.237: et quęcumque reparatione et ornatu pariter indigebant, haec largissime procurabat fecit que porticos in templo et eius ingressus ornauit, muros quoque qui ceciderunt rursus erexit turres que proceras et cibiles in eis aedificauit et in reliquis omnibus quae in regno neglecta uidebantur opus fabricationis exhibuit.
Latin.238: Qui dum ammanitis intulisset bellum atque uicisset eos annis singulis tributa praecepit ex soluere talenta auricentum, et tritica decem milia choros tantundem et hordei. Sic autem proprium ausit regnum ut hostibus quidem esset ualde terribilis. Familiaribus uero praecipue felix,
Latin.239: eo siquidem tempore fuit propheta quidam nomina autem qui de assyriorum subuersione et niniue urbi prophetans, haec dicebat niniue piscina aquae commota sic et populus omnis turbatus et fluctuatus commouebitur fugiens cunctis dicentibus ad alterutros state et manete aurumque uobis argentumque diripiente,
Latin.240: et nullus hanc uoluntatem habebit dum animas suas omnes magis quam facultates saluare festinent. Crudelis enim alterutris decertatio habebit et luctus et solatio magna membrorum et uultus eorum terrore pallescunt.
Latin.241: Ubi tunc erit habitaculum leonum. Dicit autem tibi deus niniue quando exterminabo te et nequaquam progredientes ex te imperabunt mundum.
Latin.242: Super haec autem et multa alia praedixit iste propheta de niniue quae dicere necessarium non putaui, ne legentibus uiderer et inportunus ostendi, haec autem omnia prouenerunt in niniue post annos centum et quindecim. De his ergo nunc a nobis sufficienter expositum est.
Latin.243: Porro ioacham mutauit uitam cum uixisset annis unum et quadraginta, ex quibus regnauit sedecim. Sepultus que est in regiis monumentis uenit que regnum ad eius filium achaz, qui impius circa deum existens, et paternas praeuaricator leges reges israhelitarum imitatus in hierosolimis idolorum aras instituit, et super eas sacrificauit in quibus etiam suum holocaustum obtulit filium more chananeorum, et super haec multa alia scelera perpetrauit.
Latin.244: Dumque circa haec extiterit castra metatus est aduersus eum syrorum et damascenorum rex rasen et falceas israhelitarum. Erant enim amici et reclaudentes eum in hierosolimis multis eam temporibus obsedebant, propter murorum munitionem eam capere non ualentes.
Latin.245: Syrorum uero rex capiens ciuitatem achilach ad mare rubrum positam, et habitatores eius occidens in eas uiros statuens et aliis in circuitu ciuitatibus ita fecit, perimens ubique iudaeos qui multam deuehens praedam in damascum cum suo remeauit exercitu.
Latin.246: Rex autem hierosolimorum cognoscens syros ad propria remeasse et credens praeualere contra israhelitarum regem exercitum suum aduersum eum armauit, et congressus bellum faciente ira dei deuictus est propter impietates suas multas et maximas.
Latin.247: Ea namque die centum et triginta milia eius milites ab israheliti occisi sunt et amasias princeps militię. Zachariam filium regis achaz in bello permit et tutorem totius regni ericam et principem militiae tribus iudam nomen elicam captiuum tulit. Ex tribu beniamin mulieres et infantes multamque simul deripientes praedam in samariam sunt reuersi.
Latin.248: Quidam uero odidas illius temporis propheta cum esset in samaria exercitui ante muros occurrens magna uoce clamauit dicens uictoriam eis non propria uitute conlatam sed propter iram dei quam habuit super achaz regem,
Latin.249: culpauit que eos cur ei non sufficeret sua felicitas sed etiam praesumpserint, et tribu iuda et beniamin cognatos suos captiuos adducere, suasit que illis ut eos continuo sinerent ad propria remeare, qui si non oboedirent, deo subderentur repentes solidosplido.
Latin.250: Populus igitur israhelitarum in eo conueniens quod de his fieret cogitabat. Tunc quidem barathias nom cum esset in re publica probatissimus surgens in medio et cum eo tres alii dixerunt, non est permittendum ut captiui in urbem introducantur, ne omnes a deo pariter pereamus. Sufficiant prima peccata sicu prophetae dicunt et non nouas impietates adiciamus.
Latin.251: Haec ergo milites audientes permiserunt eis ut facerent quodcumque crederent expedire. Sumentes ergo praedicti uiri captiuos lauantesque et diligentiam exhibentes et itineris dantes expensas innoxios ad propria remiserunt. Nihil omninus et illi quattuor uenire cum eis et usque ad hiericho deducentes eos non procul ab hierosolimis in samaria sunt reuersi.
Latin.252: Rex autem achaz hęc passus ab israhelitis mittens ad regem assyriorum theclapha rum poposcit ab eo belli solacium aduersus israhelitas et syros et damascenos multas pecunias se ei daturum esse promittens, misit que ei et munera ualde praeclara,
Latin.253: ille uero legatis ad se uenientibus uenit in auxilium regis achaz et castra metatus aduersus syros et regionem eorum depopulatus est, et damascum bellico iure coepit in super et regem rasen occidit. Damascenos autem in superiorem mediam destinauit, et quosdam assyriorum et in ciuitate damascena constituit.
Latin.254: Israhelitarum uero terram nimis adfligens multos ex ea captiuos adduxit. Dum ergo haec contra syros egisset rex hierosolimorum auferens aurum quodcumque erat in regalibus thesauris pariter et argentum et quod erat in templo dei et quodquod fuit optimum ornamentum deuehens haec uenit in damascum, et secundum promissiones dedit haec assyriorum regi et gratias ei pro omnibus referens in hierosolima remeauit.
Latin.255: Hic autem rex sic fuit stultus et circa modum suae uilitatis aratione alienus qua neque dum bello conprimeretur asyris deos eorum adorare cessauit, sed in eorum ueneratione permansit quasi possint ei conferre uictoriam
Latin.256: et deuictos assyriorum denuo coepit colere deos, et omnes potius uidebatur honorare quam paternum uerumque deum cuius ira fuerat eius perditionis causa
Latin.257: qui ad tantam infaniam contemptumque dei peruenit, ut omnino clauderet templum et sollempnes offeri hostias prohiberet et ornamenta eius auferret, his igitur rebus iniuruam faciens deo mortuus est, cum uixisset annis sex et triginta ex quibus regnauit sedecim, cuius filius ezechias successit in regno.
Latin.258: Eodem uero tempore mortuus est etiam rex israhelitarum, phaca dolo cuiusdam amici nomen osiae qui tenuit regnum annis nouem, fuit que, malignus dei contemptor.
Latin.259: Contra hunc autem castra metatus est assyriorum rex salmanasser eumque cum utique osias deum non haberet propitium nec adiutorem, fecit sibimet subditum et tributa definita praecepit exsoluere.
Latin.260: Anno siquidem quarto osiae regis regnauit in hierosolimis ezechias filius achaz et abiae quae ex genere fuit ciues. Erat autem huic uiro natura benigna iusta et ualde religiosa, nihil enim aliud prius eueniens ad regnum, neque necessarium nec utilius sibimet ei subiectis arbitratus est esse, quam ut coleret dei religione, et conuocans omnem populum pariter sacerdotes et leuitas contentionem habuit apud eos dicens,
Latin.261: non ignoratis quoniam patris mei peccata qui transgressus est dei sanctam honorabilemque culturam multa et maxima mala estis experti et ab eo mensuram corrupta est, suasit que quos ipse colebat deos suos pariter adorare.
Latin.262: Horto itaque uos post quam opere cognouistis quoniam pessimum est impie ut illorum obliuionem habentes purgetis uos aperiore pollutione et cum sacerdotibus atque leuitis conuenientes aperietis templum et purgantes eum sollempnibus sacrificiis ad honorem antiquum et patrium reuocetis. Sic enim deus uobis propitius erit et irasci super peccata uestra cessauit,
Latin.263: haec dicente rege sacerdotes aperuerunt templum et uasa dei et pollutiones eicientes sollemnia sacrificia super altare inposuerunt. Mittens autem rex in prouinciam sibi subiectam populum ad hierosolimam conuocans in festiuitatem celebrarent azimorum. Multum namque praeterierat tempus propter iniquitatem praedictorum regum quod non fuerat actum,
Latin.264: misit pariter israhelitas inuitans ut relinquentes malam conuersationem et consuetudinem reuerterentur ad pristinam dei que culturam dicens, concedere se uenientibus in hierosolima ut azymorum festiuitatem agerent, et cum eis aepulas pariter exercerent. Haec autem dicebat monens tantum non sibi eos subiectos facere studens, si tamen nolent. Quod si uoluissent utique beati fuissent.
Latin.265: Israhelitae uero uenientibus legatis et eis regis proprii mandata nuntiantibus non solum non adquieuerunt, sed etiam legatos tamquam fatuos inriserunt pariter etiam prophetas haec monentes et praedicantes quae paterentur si ad pietatem dei conuertere nollent spreuerunt ad nouissimum conprehendentes interemerunt,
Latin.266: et neque in his solis iniquitatibus prestiterunt, ad horum quoque peiora faciebant, nec prius quieuerunt donec deus uindicans in eis hostium eos subderet dicioni. Et de istis quidem postea declarauimus.
Latin.267: Multi tamen de tribu mannasse et zabulon et isachar oboedientes munitionibus prophetarum ad pietatis iura conuersi sunt, et isti omnes ad ezechiam in hierosolimam concurrerunt ut adorarent deum
Latin.268: his autem uenientibus rex ezechias ascendens in templum cum principibus et omni populo sacrificauit pro se tauros septem et totidem arietes, et agnas septem et totidem hyrcos in ponentes manus super capita pecodum ipse rex et princeps sacerdotibus sollempnia sacrificare promiserunt,
Latin.269: et illi quidem sacrificabant et holocausta faciebant. Leuitae uero circumstantes cum musicis organos cantabant hymnos in deum atque psallebant sicut docti suerant a dauid. Reliqui uero sacerdotes tubas cum hymnis dicentibus concrepabant. His itaque factis prostratus in faciem et ipse rex et populus uniuersus adorauerunt deum.
Latin.270: Deinde sacrificauerunt boues quidem sex centos, reliqua uero pecora tri milia, et omnia quidem sacerdotes secundum legis con suetufinem complebant. In his itaque rex delectatus est epulabatur cum populo gratias agens deo.
Latin.271: Instante uero azymorum festiuitate celebrantes quod dicitur pascha alia de cetero sacrificia diebus septem exhibuerunt, populo uero propter illa quae immolata sunt donauit rex, tauros quidem tria milia, pecudum uero diuersorum septem milia, idem autem fecerunt et principes, mille namque tauros dederunt ei, et pecora mille et quadraginta.
Latin.272: Et dum hoc modo a salomonis regi tempore cęlebratio non fuisset effecta. Tunc primum splendide et largissime probabatur exhibita. Cumque festiuitas fuisset impleta egressi in prouinciam purgauerunt eam
Latin.273: sed et ciuitatem ab omnium idolorum pollutione mundauerunt. Constituit que rex cottidiana sacrificia ex eius propriis caelebrarentur inpensis, secundum legem et sacerdotibus atque leuitis dicatas dari a plebe decreuit et primitias frugum ut semper circa religionem obseruarent, et a dei cultura separari nequiuerint,
Latin.274: et populus quidem offerebat omnes fructus ut moris erat. Domus enim et cubicula rex aedificans singulis sacerdotibus et leuitis eorumque filiis et uxoribus
Latin.275: et ita ad antiquam culturam denuo sunt reuersi, haec itaque praedicto modo rex statuens bellum egit aduersus palestinos eisque deuictis tenuit omnes ciuitates hostium agaza usque in geth. Rex autem assyriorum mittens ad eum interminatus est omnem se eius subuertere principatum, nisi tributa quae pater eius prius dabat exsolueret.
Latin.276: Ezechias autem de interminationibus non curabat, securus de pietate dei et de prophetae esaiae a quo futura omnia cognoscebat. Et de hoc quidem rege haec in praesenti dicta sufficiant.
Latin.277: Salmanasis autem assyriorum rex dum ei nuntiatum fuisset quia israhelitarum rex osiae latenter misisset ad susam aegyptiorum regem petens contra eum ab eo solacia iratus castra metatus est in samariam. Anno septimo regis osiae
Latin.278: et dum eum rex suscipere noluisset annis tribus obsidens samariam coepit eam. Nono quidem anno regni osiae septimo ezechiae regis hierosolimorum et israhelitarum uehementer exterminauit, et omnem populum transmigrauit in mediam persidam, inter quos et regem osiam uiuum coepit atque admigrauit,
Latin.279: aliasque gentes ex quodam loco nomine aut hi qui ex flumine persico uocantur in samaria, et israhelitica regione constituitur.
Latin.280: Migrauerunt ergo decem tribus israhelitarum de iudaea post annis numero non gentos quadraginta et septem. A quo tempore egridentes aegypto maiores eorum hanc tenuere prouinciam sub principe iesu. Ex quo autem recedentes aroboa qui fuit ex genere dauid. Regnum hieroboam tradiderunt sicut et prius ame significatum est, anni tunc erant ducenti et quadraginta, et menses septem et dies septem,
Latin.281: hic ergo finis adprehendit israhelitas transgredientes leges atque prophetis non oboedientes qui eis hanc praedixere calamitatem nec ab insipientibus recedentes.
Latin.282: Coepit autem malorum eorum causa fabricari, exquo seditione facta circa roboam nepotem dauid hieroboam eius serui fecerunt regem qui in deum peccando fecit eum populis uniuersis inimicum imitantibus suum malum, et ille quidem quam dignus erat exsoluit peonam.
Latin.283: Rex autem assyriorum inuasit pugnando cunctam syriam et phenicem uniuersam. Nomen autem regis huius in archiuis tyri conscriptum est. Pugnauit enim aduersus tyrum in ea regnauit heliseus de quibus testatur et menander qui temporum facta conscripsit, et tyrorum antiquitatem in grecam linguam conuertens sic ait,
Latin.284: heliseus nomen regnauit annis triginta et septem, hic recedentibus cetheis nauigans reduxit contra quos denuo salmanasser asyriorum rex insurgens cunctam phenicem inuasit, qui facta pace cum omnibus posterga sua reuersus est.
Latin.285: Recessit autem ad tyro ciuitas sidon et arche et antiqua propter tyris non subiectis, denuo rex aduersus eos egressus est phenicis exhibentibus ei naues sexaginta et remiges octuaginta,
Latin.286: contra quos tyri nauigantes in duodecim nauibus dispersis hostium nauibus coepere captiuos uiros quingentos. Unde honor tyrorum propter haec creuit eximiae.
Latin.287: Reuertens autem assyriorum rex disposuit custodias superfluum et aqua ducta ciuium, ut tyrios aurire pocula prohiberent. Et dum hoc quinque annis suisset factum, tulerunt de ex fosis puteis habentes aquam. Haec ita in archiuis tyris de salmanasso assyriorum rege conscripta sunt.
Latin.288: Igitur dum fuissent in samaria transmigrauit huthei, hoc enim uocabulo actenus uocabantur, eo quod a prouincia persida et a quodam flumine quae cutha uocatur migrati uiderentur, singuli eorum secundum gentem propriam deos in samariam portauerunt.
Latin.289: Uenit que pestilentia super super eos per quam corrupti cum nullam malorum medicinam inuenire possent deum maximum colere pro salute coeperunt. Mittentes itaque se ad regem assyriorum legatos supplicauerunt ut sacerdotes eis ex captiuis israhelitarum quos pugnando teneuerat destinaret,
Latin.290: quo mittente sacerdotes legis et dei culturam eos edocuerunt, et dum coepissent eum summa deuotione uenerare, pestilentia repente cessauit, et actenus ipsas sollempnitates celebrare noscuntur his siquidem secundum eloquium hebraeorum cuthei secundum genere. Grece autem samaritiae uocantur,
Latin.291: propter rerum motum semper parati sunt, et quando uident iudeos esse felices cognatos eos appellent, et quasi de ioseph nati uideantur, et ex illo cum eis habeant societatis initium. Quando uero deiectos uident, nequaquam eis deuotione aut genere communicare uolunt, sed et transmigratos, et alienigenas semetipsos dicunt, et de his quidem oportunus edicemus.

EnglishContext.1: WHEN Jehoshaphat the king was come to Jerusalem, from the assistance he had afforded Ahab, the king of Israel, when he fought with Benhadad, king of Syria, the prophet Jehu met him, and accused him for assisting Ahab, a man both impious and wicked; and said to him, that God was displeased with him for so doing, but that he delivered him from the enemy, notwithstanding he had sinned, because of his own proper disposition, which was good. Whereupon the king betook himself to thanksgivings and sacrifices to God; after which he presently went over all that country which he ruled round about, and taught the people, as well the laws which God gave them by Moses, as that religious worship that was due to him. He also constituted judges in every one of the cities of his kingdom; and charged them to have regard to nothing so much in judging the multitude as to do justice, and not to be moved by bribes, nor by the dignity of men eminent for either their riches or their high birth, but to distribute justice equally to all, as knowing that God is conscious of every secret action of theirs. When he had himself instructed them thus, and gone over every city of the two tribes, he returned to Jerusalem. He there also constituted judges out of the priests and the Levites, and principal persons of the multitude, and admonished them to pass all their sentences with care and justice And that if any of the people of his country had differences of great consequence, they should send them out of the other cities to these judges, who would be obliged to give righteous sentences concerning such causes; and this with the greater care, because it is proper that the sentences which are given in that city wherein the temple of God is, and wherein the king dwells, be given with great care and the utmost justice. Now he set over them Amariah the priest, and Zebadiah, [both] of the tribe of Judah; and after this manner it was that the king ordered these affairs.

EnglishContext.7: About the same time the Moabites and Ammonites made an expedition against Jehoshaphat, ,and took with them a great body of Arabians, and pitched their camp at Engedi, a city that is situate at the lake Asphaltiris, and distant three hundred furlongs from Jerusalem. In that place grows the best kind of palm trees, and the opobalsamum. Now Jehoshaphat heard that the enemies had passed over the lake, and had made an irruption into that country which belonged to his kingdom; at which news he was aftrighted, and called the people of Jerusalem to a congregation in the temple, and standing over against the temple itself, he called upon God to afford him power and strength, so as to inflict punishment on those that made this expedition against them (for that those who built this his temple had prayed, that he would protect that city, and take vengeance on those that were so bold as to come against it); for they are come to take from us that land which thou hast given us for a possession. When he had prayed thus, he fell into tears; and the whole multitude, together with their wives and children, made their supplications also: upon which a certain prophet, Jahaziel by name, came into the midst of the assembly, and cried out, and spake both to the multitude and to the king, that God heard their prayers, and promised to fight against their enemies. He also gave order that the king should draw his forces out the next day, for that he should find them between Jerusalem and the ascent of Engedi, at a place called The Eminence, and that he should not fight against them, but only stand still, and see how God would fight against them. When the prophet had said this, both the king and the multitude fell upon their faces, and gave thanks to God, and worshipped him; and the Levites continued singing hymns to God with their instruments of music.

EnglishContext.12: As soon as it was day, and the king was come into that wilderness which is under the city of Tekoa, he said to the multitude, "that they ought to give credit to what the prophet had said, and not to set themselves in array for fighting; but to set the priests with their trumpets, and the Levites with the singers of hymns, to give thanks to God, as having already delivered our country from our enemies." This opinion of the king pleased [the people], and they did what he advised them to do. So God caused a terror and a commotion to arise among the Ammonites, who thought one another to be enemies, and slew one another, insomuch that not one man out of so great an army escaped; and when Jehoshaphat looked upon that valley wherein their enemies had been encamped, and saw it full of dead men, he rejoiced at so surprising an event, as was this assistance of God, while he himself by his own power, and without their labor, had given them the victory. He also gave his army leave to take the prey of the enemy's camp, and to spoil their dead bodies; and indeed so they did for three days together, till they were weary, so great was the number of the slain; and on the fourth day, all the people were gathered together unto a certain hollow place or valley, and blessed God for his power and assistance, from which the place had this name given it, the Valley of [Berachah, or] Blessing.

So God caused a terror and a commotion to arise among the Ammonites, who thought one another to be enemies, and slew one another, insomuch that not one man out of so great an army escaped; and when Jehoshaphat looked upon that valley wherein their enemies had been encamped, and saw it full of dead men, he rejoiced at so surprising an event, as was this assistance of God, while he himself by his own power, and without their labor, had given them the victory. He also gave his army leave to take the prey of the enemy's camp, and to spoil their dead bodies; and indeed so they did for three days together, till they were weary, so great was the number of the slain; and on the fourth day, all the people were gathered together unto a certain hollow place or valley, and blessed God for his power and assistance, from which the place had this name given it, the Valley of [Berachah, or] Blessing.
EnglishContext.16: And when the king had brought his army back to Jerusalem, he betook himself to celebrate festivals, and offer sacrifices, and this for many days. And indeed, after this destruction of their enemies, and when it came to the ears of the foreign nations, they were all greatly aftrighted, as supposing that God would openly fight for him hereafter. So Jehoshaphat from that time lived in great glory and splendor, on account of his righteousness and his piety towards God. He was also in friendship with Ahab's son, who was king of Israel; and he joined with him in the building of ships that were to sail to Pontus, and the traffic cities of Thrace but he failed of his gains, for the ships were destroyed by being so great [and unwieldy]; on which account he was no longer concerned about shipping. And this is the history of Jehoshaphat, the king of Jerusalem.

EnglishContext.18: AND now Ahaziah, the son of Ahab, reigned over Israel, and made his abode in Samaria. He was a wicked man, and in all respects like to both his parents and to Jeroboam, who first of all transgressed, and began to deceive the people. In the second year of his reign, the king of Moab fell off from his obedience, and left off paying those tributes which he before paid to his father Ahab. Now it happened that Ahaziah, as he was coming down from the top of his house, fell down from it, and in his sickness sent to the Fly, which was the god of Ekron, for that was this god's name, to inquire about his recovery but the God of the Hebrews appeared to Elijah the prophet, and commanded him to go and meet the messengers that were sent, and to ask them, whether the people of Israel had pot a God of their own, that the king sent to a foreign god to inquire about his recovery? and to bid them return and tell the king that he would not escape this disease. And when Elijah had performed what God had commanded him, and the messengers had heard what he said, they returned to the king immediately; and when the king wondered how they could return so soon, and asked them the reason of it, they said that a certain man met them, and forbade them to go on any farther; but to return and tell thee, from the command of the God of Israel, that this disease will have a bad end. And when the king bid them describe the man that said this to them, they replied that he was a hairy man, and was girt about with a girdle of leather. So the king understood by this that the man who was described by the messengers was Elijah; whereupon he sent a captain to him, with fifty soldiers, and commanded them to bring Elijah to him; and when the captain that was sent found Elijah sitting upon the top of a hill, he commanded him to come down, and to come to the king, for so had he enjoined; but that in case he refused, they would carry him by force. Elijah said to him, "That you may have a trial whether I be a true prophet, I will pray that fire may fall from heaven, and destroy both the soldiers and yourself." So he prayed, and a whirlwind of fire fell [from heaven], and destroyed the captain, and those that were with him. And when the king was informed of the destruction of these men, he was very angry, and sent another captain with the like number of armed men that were sent before. And when this captain also threatened the prophet, that unless he came down of his own accord, he would take him and carry him away, upon his prayer against him, the fire [from heaven] slew this captain as well the other. And when, upon inquiry, the king was informed of what happened to him, he sent out a third captain. But when this captain, who was a wise man, and of a mild disposition, came to the place where Elijah happened to be, and spake civilly to him; and said that he knew that it was without his own consent, and only in submission to the king's command that he came to him; and that those that came before did not come willingly, but on the same account; — he therefore desired him to have pity on those armed men that were with him, and that he would come down and follow him to the king. So Elijah accepted of his discreet words and courteous behavior, and came down and followed him. And when he came to the king, he prophesied to him and told him that God said, "Since thou hast despised him as not being God, and so unable to foretell the truth about thy distemper, but hast sent to the god of Ekron to inquire of him what will be the end of this thy distemper, know this, that thou shalt die."

So the king understood by this that the man who was described by the messengers was Elijah; whereupon he sent a captain to him, with fifty soldiers, and commanded them to bring Elijah to him; and when the captain that was sent found Elijah sitting upon the top of a hill, he commanded him to come down, and to come to the king, for so had he enjoined; but that in case he refused, they would carry him by force. Elijah said to him, "That you may have a trial whether I be a true prophet, I will pray that fire may fall from heaven, and destroy both the soldiers and yourself." So he prayed, and a whirlwind of fire fell [from heaven], and destroyed the captain, and those that were with him. And when the king was informed of the destruction of these men, he was very angry, and sent another captain with the like number of armed men that were sent before. And when this captain also threatened the prophet, that unless he came down of his own accord, he would take him and carry him away, upon his prayer against him, the fire [from heaven] slew this captain as well the other. And when, upon inquiry, the king was informed of what happened to him, he sent out a third captain. But when this captain, who was a wise man, and of a mild disposition, came to the place where Elijah happened to be, and spake civilly to him; and said that he knew that it was without his own consent, and only in submission to the king's command that he came to him; and that those that came before did not come willingly, but on the same account; — he therefore desired him to have pity on those armed men that were with him, and that he would come down and follow him to the king. So Elijah accepted of his discreet words and courteous behavior, and came down and followed him. And when he came to the king, he prophesied to him and told him that God said, "Since thou hast despised him as not being God, and so unable to foretell the truth about thy distemper, but hast sent to the god of Ekron to inquire of him what will be the end of this thy distemper, know this, that thou shalt die."
EnglishContext.27: Accordingly the king in a very little time died, as Elijah had foretold; but Jehoram his brother succeeded him in the kingdom, for he died without children: but for this Jehoram, he was like his father Ahab in wickedness, and reigned twelve years, indulging himself in all sorts of wickedness and impiety towards God, for, leaving off his worship, he worshipped foreign gods; but in other respects he was an active man. Now at this time it was that Elijah disappeared from among men, and no one knows of his death to this very day; but he left behind him his disciple Elisha, as we have formerly declared. And indeed, as to Elijah, and as to Enoch, who was before the deluge, it is written in the sacred books that they disappeared, but so that nobody knew that they died.

EnglishContext.29: WHEN Joram had taken upon him the kingdom, he determined to make an expedition against the king of Moab, whose name was Mesha; for, as we told you before, he was departed from his obedience to his brother [Ahaziah], while he paid to his father Ahab two hundred thousand sheep, with their fleeces of wool. When therefore he had gathered his own army together, he sent also to Jehoshaphat, and entreated him, that since he had from the beginning been a friend to his father, he would assist him in the war that he was entering into against the Moabites, who had departed from their obedience, who not only himself promised to assist him, but would also oblige the king of Edom, who was under his authority, to make the same expedition also. When Joram had received these assurances of assistance from Jehoshaphat, he took his army with him, and came to Jerusalem; and when he had been sumptuously entertained by the king of Jerusalem, it was resolved upon by them to take their march against their enemies through the wilderness of Edom. And when they had taken a compass of seven days' journey, they were in distress for want of water for the cattle, and for the army, from the mistake of their roads by the guides that conducted them, insomuch that they were all in an agony, especially Joram; and cried to God, by reason of their sorrow, and [desired to know] what wickedness had been committed by them that induced him to deliver three kings together, without fighting, unto the king of Moab. But Jehoshaphat, who was a righteous man, encouraged him, and bade him send to the camp, and know whether any prophet of God was come along with them, that we might by him learn from God what we should do. And when one of the servants of Joram said that he had seen there Elisha, the son of Shaphat, the disciple of Elijah, the three kings went to him, at the entreaty of Jehoshaphat; and when they were come at the prophet's tent, which tent was pitched out of the camp, they asked him what would become of the army? and Joram was particularly very pressing with him about it. And when he replied to him, that he should not trouble him, but go to his father's and mother's prophets, for they [to be sure] were true prophets, he still desired him to prophesy, and to save them. So he swore by God that he would not answer him, unless it were on account of Jehoshaphat, who was a holy and righteous man; and when, at his desire, they brought him a man that could play on the psaltery, the Divine Spirit came upon him as the music played, and he commanded them to dig many trenches in the valley; for, said he, "though there appear neither cloud, nor wind, nor storm of rain, ye shall see this river full of water, till the army and the cattle be saved for you by drinking of it. Nor will this be all the favor that you shall receive from God, but you shall also overcome your enemies, and take the best and strongest cities of the Moabites, and you shall cut down their fruit trees, and lay waste their country, and stop up their fountains and rivers."

EnglishContext.37: When the prophet had said this, the next day, before the sun-rising, a great torrent ran strongly; for God had caused it to rain very plentifully at the distance of three days' journey into Edom, so that the army and the cattle found water to drink in abundance. But when the Moabites heard that the three kings were coming upon them, and made their approach through the wilderness, the king of Moab gathered his army together presently, and commanded them to pitch their camp upon the mountains, that when the enemies should attempt to enter their country, they might not be concealed from them. But when at the rising of the sun they saw the water in the torrent, for it was not far from the land of Moab, and that it was of the color of blood, for at such a time the water especially looks red, by the shining of the sun upon it, they formed a false notion of the state of their enemies, as if they had slain one another for thirst; and that the river ran with their blood. However, supposing that this was the case, they desired their king would send them out to spoil their enemies; whereupon they all went in haste, as to an advantage already gained, and came to the enemy's camp, as supposing them destroyed already. But their hope deceived them; for as their enemies stood round about them, some of them were cut to pieces, and others of them were dispersed, and fled to their own country. And when the kings fell into the land of Moab, they overthrew the cities that were in it, and spoiled their fields, and marred them, filling them with stones out of the brooks, and cut down the best of their trees, and stopped up their fountains of water, and overthrew their walls to their foundations. But the king of Moab, when he was pursued, endured a siege; and seeing his city in danger of being overthrown by force, made a sally, and went out with seven hundred men, in order to break through the enemy's camp with his horsemen, on that side where the watch seemed to be kept most negligently; and when, upon trial, he could not get away, for he lighted upon a place that was carefully watched, he returned into the city, and did a thing that showed despair and the utmost distress; for he took his eldest son, who was to reign after him, and lifting him up upon the wall, that he might be visible to all the enemies, he offered him as a whole burnt-offering to God, whom, when the kings saw, they commiserated the distress that was the occasion of it, and were so affected, in way of humanity and pity, that they raised the siege, and every one returned to his own house. So Jehoshaphat came to Jerusalem, and continued in peace there, and outlived this expedition but a little time, and then died, having lived in all sixty years, and of them reigned twenty-five. He was buried in a magnificent manner in Jerusalem, for he had imitated the actions of David.

EnglishContext.45: JEHOSHAPAT had a good number of children; but he appointed his eldest son Jehoram to be his successor, who had the same name with his mother's brother, that was king of Israel, and the son of Ahab. Now when the king of Israel was come out of the land of Moab to Samaria, he had with him Elisha the prophet, whose acts I have a mind to go over particularly, for they were illustrious, and worthy to be related, as we have them set down in the sacred books.

EnglishContext.47: For they say that the widow of Obadiah Ahab's steward, came to him, and said, that he was not ignorant how her husband had preserved the prophets that were to be slain by Jezebel, the wife of Ahab; for she said that he hid a hundred of them, and had borrowed money for their maintenance, and that, after her husband's death, she and her children were carried away to be made slaves by the creditors; and she desired of him to have mercy upon her on account of what her husband did, and afford her some assistance. And when he asked her what she had in the house, she said, "Nothing but a very small quantity of oil in a cruse." So the prophet bid her go away, and borrow a great many empty vessels of her neighbors, and when she had shut her chamber door, to pour the oil into them all; for that God would fill them full. And when the woman had done what she was commanded to do, and bade her children bring every one of the vessels, and all were filled, and not one left empty, she came to the prophet, and told him that they were all full; upon which he advised her to go away, and sell the oil, and pay the creditors what was owing them, for that there would be some surplus of the price of the oil, which she might make use of for the maintenance of her children. And thus did Elisha discharge the woman's debts, and free her from the vexation of her creditors.

EnglishContext.110: But Jehu came out, and went to the place where he before sat with the captains; and when they asked him, and desired him to tell them, wherefore it was that this young man came to him, and added withal that he was mad, he replied, —"You guess right, for the words he spake were the words of a madman;" and when they were eager about the matter, and desired he would tell them, he answered, that God had said he had chosen him to be king over the multitude. When he had said this, every one of them put off his garment, and strewed it under him, and blew with trumpets, and gave notice that Jehu was king. So when he had gotten the army together, he was preparing to set out immediately against Joram, at the city Jezreel, in which city, as we said before, he was healing of the wound which he had received in the siege of Ramoth.
